notes: §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR16: "When the EXTEND phrase is specified and the LABEL RECORDS clause indicates label records are present, the execution of the OPEN statement includes the following steps": a to c process the beginning and the ending labels as an INPUT open would, and d is "Processing then proceeds as though the file has been opened with the OUTPUT phrase." The label steps are the implementor's (§1985:C.2, item 61: "The labels are checked or written in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input or output label handling."; §1985:VII.3.6.3 GR2: the labels "conform to the implementor's label specifications"). The implementation's convention is that a file carries no label the COBOL program can see: labels belong to the host file system (§1985:C.1: "Specifying the presence of file labels is considered a function of the operating system and as such does not belong in the COBOL program"), and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md Table 7 row 7.4 states the clause 'accepted-inert at 85'. The clause is parsed at 85 (FileDescriptionFormats.Rows admits it in every FD format; VisitLabelRecordsClause refuses it from 2002, COBOL0902) and no binder, emitter or runtime member reads it, so steps a to c have no action and the EXTEND arm of SequentialConnector.OpenCore is step d: it opens the writer in append mode after the last record (§1985:VII.4.3.4 GR15) and the WRITE statements that follow add records as an output file's do. Probed at --std 85 on one host file through three file-names: OPEN EXTEND under LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD, under LABEL RECORD IS OMITTED and with no clause each answer 00 and append after the existing records, and the file holds the records alone (16 bytes for four 4-character records, no label bytes). The witness writes one record, extends the LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD file with a second and reads both back in order. Not covered by this verdict: the clause's own syntax is unchecked at 85 (kb/Work PB5070), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no entry for the label items of the 1985 implementor-defined list, so the convention is written down only in the VCR row.

next.reason: 1985: "When the EXTEND phrase is specified and the LABEL RECORDS clause indicates label records are present, ... file labels are processed"; 2023: "GR-14.9.27.4-15 only positions the file 'immediately after the last logical record'; no candidate mentions label records or labels". The 2023 EXTEND rules cover positioning and the volume pointer but say nothing of label processing. The LABEL RECORDS feature and its label steps are not carried.
